clinical_features.symptoms:
Symptoms: Nausea, Vomiting, dehydration, lethargy, weakness, muscle 
irritability (twitching, seizures), ataxia, drowsiness, stupor, coma 
Pathophysiology: water depletion and/or solute excess 
 
Equations: Calculated serum osmolality = (2 x sNa+) + glucose + urea 
Free water deficit: 0.6 x Weight(kg) x [(sNa+ – 140)/140] 
5DW or half normal saline infusion rate: Use MDCalc 
 
General Approach if critically Ill: 
- ABC’s, Monitors, IV, ECG, urine catheter 
- Shock/Dehydration ➔ fluid resuscitation 1st priority using isotonic solutions e.g. Balsol / RL (relatively hypotonic compared to serum) 
- Estimate fluid deficit and infuse 5% dextrose water or half-normal saline over 48 hours. 
- Aim to correct Na+ by 10-12mmol/l in 24hrs (Not more than 0.5mmol/l/hour) ➔ DO NOT CORRECT TOO FAST FOR RISK OF CEREBRAL OEDEMA. 
- Tap water can also be given orally or via NGT. 
- Investigate and treat cause 
 
Causes of Hypernatraemia 
Hypernatraemia 
 
Extra-Cellular Fluid Status 
 
Hypovolaemia/Dehydration 
 
Na+ <<< H2O Loss 
1) Renal Losses (uNa+ > 20 mmol/l) 
Diuretics eg furosemide 
Osmotic Diuresis 
2) Extra-renal Losses (uNa+ < 10 mmol/l) 
Sweating, Diarrhea, Vomiting, Burns 
Isovolaemia 
Mild to Moderate H2O Loss 
1) Renal H2O Loss (uOsm < 700mOsm/l) 
Diabetes Insipidus (central or nephrogenic) 
2) Extra-renal H2O Loss (uOsm > 700mOsm/l) 
insensible losses, hypodipsia 
Hypervolaemia/Oedema 
 
Na+ >>> H20 Retention 
1) Mineralocorticoid Excess: 
Cushing Syndrome 
Hyperaldosteronsim 
2) Exogenous: 
Salt water intake 
Hypertonic Saline/NaBicarb 
 
 
Replace H2O AND Na+: 
Initially Isotonic fluid e.g. Ringers 
Lactate until euvolaemic, then 
5DW or Oral Free water 
Replace H20: 
5DW or Oral free water 
If Diabetes Insipidus: 
Central: Treat with DDAVP* 1-2µg 
IM/SC/IV 
Nephrogenic: Fluid Restriction, 
DDAVP*, HCTZ 
Remove Na+ AND H2O: 
Diuretics e.g. furosemide 
and replace losses with 
5DW or oral free water to 
achieve negative balance
